research_task: Determine whether older project research contains mechanisms that materially alter the current G1c ClayGraph candidate.

questions.q: What older mechanism preserves the original goal that memory influences the next thought before explicit retrieval?
Did older Clay research already specify an update path compatible with a resident graph?
Does the historical architecture require one physical graph database?
gold: no; physically plural storage allowed behind one logical world

retrieval_observation: Broad historical search surfaced relevant XENO/ClayCode material but required staged opening and synthesis. A recent-upload navigation search surfaced the exact memory-transcendence text. This is useful process evidence, not a graph-vs-search benchmark.
decision_effect: Yes. Historical recovery changed the candidate from G1c query-time resident adaptive escalation to G1d epochal latent field by restoring continuous between-call activation and adding update/epoch semantics.
blocked_comparison: The actual repository ClayGraph/G1d runtime cannot be executed from this connector surface, so no claim is made that G1d retrieval outperforms File Library/FTS. Promotion remains HOLD.
